note: A synthetic client (Slice 129 worked example). Not a real company.
problem: Claims on our pet insurance book came in at $6.3 million last year against earned premium of $9 million.

answers.common.decision: Whether to propose a rate increase; our appointed actuary signs off any rate or reserve change.
answers.common.deadline: Rate filings for next year are due in two months.
answers.common.audience: The appointed actuary and the head of pricing.
answers.common.materials: We priced the book for a loss ratio of 60%. Claim counts rose from 4,000 to 4,500, and the average claim rose from $1,200 to $1,400.
answers.finance-modeling.purpose: Explain why the loss ratio missed its target and size the gap.
answers.finance-modeling.data: Last year's claims and premium by month, with claim counts and average claim size, in US dollars.
